threads.body: [Javaagent] This matcher now also selects `write(byte[], int, int)`, applying both byte-array advices to that overload. In both Servlet 3 and Servlet 5, the whole-array advice passes `0, write.length` to the snippet-injection helper instead of the requested offset and length. With injection enabled, a `<head>` outside the requested slice can cause the entire backing buffer to be written and the original sliced write to be skipped, corrupting the response or exposing unused buffer contents. Restore `takesArguments(1)` here to keep the overloads disjoint.

@copilot Please fix all of the following on this PR's existing branch.

- In `CouchbaseProtostellarCoreInstrumentation.java`, restrict `CoreConstructorAdvice` to constructors declared by `com.couchbase.client.core.Core`, using `.and(isDeclaredBy(named("com.couchbase.client.core.Core")))`. The current matcher also selects the supported Couchbase 3.4.3 `CoreProtostellar(Core, Authenticator, Set)` constructor. `CoreProtostellar` does not extend `Core`, so `@Advice.This Core` is incompatible. Keep the legacy constructor advice separate. This fixes the open review finding without restoring an unused-argument type constraint.
- In the Google HTTP client module's `GoogleHttpRequestInstrumentation.java`, restore the static `ElementMatchers.takesArguments` import. The synchronous `execute` matcher still calls `takesArguments(0)` and currently fails compilation.
- In Lettuce 4's `LettuceObservableCommandInstrumentation.java`, restore the static `ElementMatchers.takesArgument` import. The throwable matcher still calls `takesArgument(0, Throwable.class)` and currently fails compilation.
- In Kafka's `KafkaConsumerInstrumentation.java`, remove the unused `java.time.Duration` import. Error Prone reports it and `-Werror` fails compilation.
- In Vert.x SQL client 5's `ConnectionFactoryInstrumentation.java`, remove the unused static `ElementMatchers.takesArguments` import. This also fails compilation under `-Werror`.
- Apply scoped Spotless tasks to the modules changed by this PR. The current Spotless job first fails on `ActivejAsyncServletInstrumentation.java`, where the simplified `serve` matcher should fit on one line. Because the job stops at its first violation, there may be more formatting issues in the touched files.

Compile the affected modules and run the existing installed-agent Couchbase 3.4.3 and 3.4.4 tests, including `version343Test` and `version344Test`. Recheck CI after these fixes. The current build, test, latest-dependency, smoke-test, examples, and muzzle failures largely cascade from the compilation blockers above; do not treat each red job as an independent runtime bug.

Keep the agreed batch rule: remove type constraints on arguments the advice does not use, and remove argument-count constraints that are unnecessary for advice compatibility or selecting the intended supported methods. Argument use includes `AllArguments`, helper calls, descriptor interpretation, and argument replacement. Relaxing constraints on used `Object` arguments remains outside this batch.

Preserve the PR's current title, description, and ready-for-review state. Leave existing review threads unresolved.

@copilot Please fix the remaining ClassLoader CI regression on this PR's existing branch. Add `.and(takesArguments(5))` to this byte-array `defineClass` matcher and restore the static import for `takesArguments`. Keep the unused `ProtectionDomain` type check removed.

The current matcher selects both `defineClass(String, byte[], int, int)` and `defineClass(String, byte[], int, int, ProtectionDomain)`. The four-argument wrapper delegates to the five-argument overload, so the advice invokes `beforeDefineClass` twice for one class definition. This is an argument-count constraint we must retain to select the intended method and avoid double advice on a delegating wrapper.

In https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/actions/runs/38989325638/job/117268182158, `DefineClassInstrumentationTest.ensureDefineClassInstrumented` fails for `byteArray4` on every retry with `TooManyActualInvocations`: one `beforeDefineClass` invocation expected, two received. The latest-dependency job reports the same failure. This is different from the earlier unrelated null-context exit-callback verification problem.

Keep the test's exact-once entry verification, context-specific exit verification, and successful class-definition assertions. Do not weaken the assertions to accept two callbacks or use `atLeastOnce()`. Keep this fix scoped to the byte-array matcher and its import.

Run the module's scoped Spotless apply task, then `:instrumentation:internal:internal-class-loader:javaagent:test --tests '*DefineClassInstrumentationTest'` on the repository's default JDK and recheck CI. Preserve the existing PR title, description, and ready-for-review state. Leave existing review threads unresolved.

@copilot Please replace the `takesArgument(1, any())` existence check here with an explicit `namedOneOf` matcher for the two supported connection-string types:

```java
isConstructor()
    .and(
        takesArgument(
            1,
            namedOneOf(
                "com.couchbase.client.java.ConnectionString",
                "com.couchbase.client.core.utils.ConnectionString")))
```

The first name appears in the earlier Couchbase 2.x constructors and the second in later 2.x constructors. These are the two argument types found when inspecting the cached 2.x library releases. Match their names rather than adding a custom minimum-arity lambda or retaining `any()`. The positional type matcher already guarantees argument 1 exists.

Keep `@Advice.Argument(1) Object connectionString` in the advice so it can receive either class. Do not use `takesArgument(1, Object.class)`, which would require the constructor parameter to be declared exactly as `Object`. Keep the unused boolean constraint and unnecessary exact argument count removed.

Keep this change scoped to the constructor matcher and its imports. Run the module's scoped Spotless apply task and the relevant Couchbase tests for both connection-string package eras. Preserve the PR's current title, description, and ready-for-review state, and leave existing review threads unresolved.
